references.text: Jesus returned to Cana in Galilee, "where he had turned water into wine" ([ref:Joh 4:46|John 4:46]). A direct reference to the same miracle described in John 2:9.
The six stone jars were filled with water ([ref:Joh 2:6-7|John 2:6-7]). The servants knew it was water they had drawn, unlike the master of the banquet who did not know where the wine came from.

The wind blows wherever it pleases, and "you do not know where it comes from" ([ref:Joh 3:8|John 3:8]). The same theme that God's works have an origin hidden from humans – parallel to how the master of the banquet did not know where the wine came from (πόθεν ἐστίν).

The people thought they knew where Jesus came from ([ref:Joh 7:27|John 7:27]). The question of knowing "where someone/something comes from" (πόθεν) is a recurring theme in the Gospel of John, reflecting the master of the banquet's ignorance about the origin of the wine.

The Pharisees said they did not know where Jesus came from ([ref:Joh 9:29-30|John 9:29-30]). Ignorance about the origin of Jesus' works is a recurring theme, just as the master of the banquet also did not know where the wine came from.

The water in the Nile was turned into blood as the first sign in Egypt ([ref:2 Mos 7:17-21|Exodus 7:17-21]). An Old Testament parallel to the transformation of water, but here as judgment. Jesus' sign at Cana is instead a sign of grace, transforming water into wine.

The Lord will prepare a feast with "aged wine, clear and refined" ([ref:Jes 25:6|Isaiah 25:6]). The messianic feast with abundant good wine forms the prophetic background for Jesus' miracle at the wedding, where he provides wine of the finest quality.
"Wine that gladdens the human heart" ([ref:Sal 104:15|Psalms 104:15]). The wine as God's gift to bring joy to people forms the background for Jesus' generous miracle at the wedding.

"On that day the mountains will drip with sweet wine" ([ref:Am 9:13|Amos 9:13]). The prophecy of an abundance of wine in the messianic age provides the background for Jesus' generous gift of wine at the wedding in Cana.
